meta-runner.name: Upload release metadata to S3
meta-runner.description: Uploads the download page's release metadata files to s3://mc-tca-01/releases/

param.name: release.metadata.files
param.spec: text label='Release metadata files' description='Comma-separated globs of the .xml and .json files to upload' validationMode='not_empty' display='normal'

parameters.param:
import datetime, glob, hashlib, hmac, os, ssl, sys, time, urllib.error, urllib.parse, urllib.request
# The credentials are the project's artifact storage key for this bucket access_key = r'''%release.metadata.aws.access.key.id%''' secret_key = r'''%release.metadata.aws.secret.access.key%''' file_patterns = r'''%release.metadata.files%''' bucket = "mc-tca-01" region = "us-west-2" host = bucket + ".s3." + region + ".amazonaws.com" content_types = {".xml": "text/xml", ".json": "application/json"}
try: import certifi ssl_context = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where()) except ImportError: ssl_context = None
def hmac_sha256(key, message): return hmac.new(key, message.encode("utf-8"), hashlib.sha256).digest()
# PUTs one file under releases/ with an AWS Signature Version 4, using only the standard library # so no agent needs boto3. no-cache makes browsers revalidate, so the page sees each new build. def upload(path): with open(path, "rb") as f: body = f.read() key = "releases/" + os.path.basename(path) now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None, microsecond=0) amz_date = now.isoformat().replace("-", "").replace(":", "") + "Z" scope = amz_date[:8] + "/" + region + "/s3/aws4_request" payload_hash = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest() headers = { "cache-control": "no-cache", "content-type": content_types.get(os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower(), "application/octet-stream"), "host": host, "x-amz-content-sha256": payload_hash, "x-amz-date": amz_date, } signed_headers = ";".join(sorted(headers)) canonical_request = "\n".join(["PUT", "/" + urllib.parse.quote(key), "", "".join(name + ":" + headers[name] + "\n" for name in sorted(headers)), signed_headers, payload_hash]) string_to_sign = "\n".join(["AWS4-HMAC-SHA256", amz_date, scope, hashlib.sha256(canonical_request.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()]) signing_key = ("AWS4" + secret_key).encode("utf-8") for scope_part in scope.split("/"): signing_key = hmac_sha256(signing_key, scope_part) signature = hmac.new(signing_key, string_to_sign.encode("utf-8"), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest() headers["authorization"] = ("AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Credential=" + access_key + "/" + scope + ", SignedHeaders=" + signed_headers + ", Signature=" + signature) del headers["host"] # urllib sends it from the URL request = urllib.request.Request("https://" + host + "/" + urllib.parse.quote(key), data=body, headers=headers, method="PUT") # Network errors and 5xx responses are retried; a 4xx (bad credentials, access denied) is not attempts = 3 for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1): try: with urllib.request.urlopen(request, context=ssl_context, timeout=60) as response: print("Uploaded " + path + " to s3://" + bucket + "/" + key + " (HTTP " + str(response.status) + ")") return except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: if e.code < 500 or attempt == attempts: # S3's error body names the cause, e.g. AccessDenied, SignatureDoesNotMatch or RequestTimeTooSkewed raise RuntimeError(str(e) + ": " + e.read().decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()) from e print("Attempt " + str(attempt) + " to upload " + key + " failed: " + str(e)) except OSError as e: if attempt == attempts: raise print("Attempt " + str(attempt) + " to upload " + key + " failed: " + str(e)) time.sleep(10 * attempt)
paths = sorted(set(path for pattern in file_patterns.split(",") if pattern.strip() for path in glob.glob(pattern.strip()) if os.path.isfile(path))) failures = 0 if paths else 1 if not paths: print("No release metadata files match: " + file_patterns) for path in paths: try: upload(path) except Exception as e: failures += 1 print("Failed to upload " + path + ": " + str(e))
# The download page reads only this copy, so a failed upload fails the build if failures: sys.exit("Release metadata was not uploaded to S3; see the errors above")
